trust_decision.summary: Whether a model-supplied path/glob pattern (and every file it expands to, after symlink resolution) stays inside the configured root_path / allowed virtual prefix; decided in FilesystemFileSearchMiddleware (_validate_and_resolve_path validates only the base `path`, never the glob `pattern` or per-match resolved paths) and in langchain_anthropic's _validate_path / _FilesystemClaudeFileToolMiddleware._validate_and_resolve_path (raw str.startswith prefix test, not segment-aware).

landing_point.why: The summary says 'path traversal in file-search middleware'; the only visible traversal guard is _validate_and_resolve_path, which already rejects '..'/'~' and resolves the base path, so an engineer looks there first and may conclude the base path is fine without noticing the glob `pattern` and symlinked matches bypass it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report points at langchain_v1 file-search; the Anthropic text-editor/memory tools are a different partner package whose filesystem variant already resolves and root-contains the path (anthropic_tools.py:839-846), so the prefix check looks like a cosmetic namespacing feature rather than a security boundary; and the Python grep fallback 'only runs when ripgrep is unavailable'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate in-root results must keep working: glob '*.py' / '**/...' patterns and file names containing '..' as a substring (fix only rejects whole '..' segments), in-root symlinks whose target is inside root, the exact prefix directory '/memories' itself and its descendants, and the 'No files found'/'No matches found' return contract instead of raising. An over-broad fix (reject any '..' substring in pattern, drop all symlinks, require trailing-slash prefix match) breaks these.
